hint_ladder.title: Orient
hint_ladder.text: This word is all about group harmony. Think of a team that has talked things through and everyone is on the same page. What's that feeling called?

hint_ladder.title: Apply
hint_ladder.text: Imagine a family deciding where to eat. Everyone agrees on pizza—that's consensus. Look at options: which one captures 'everyone agrees'?

hint_ladder.title: Nearly Give Away
hint_ladder.text: 'Consensus' comes from Latin 'to feel together.' So the answer is the option meaning 'general agreement.' That's C.

A.text: You might have chosen A because you mistook 'consensus' for 'disagreement,' but it's actually the opposite—general harmony.

B.text: You might have chosen B because majority vote feels like group agreement, but consensus requires everyone, not just over half.

C.text: Correct. General agreement is exactly what consensus means—a shared feeling of agreement within a group.

D.text: You might have chosen D because debate involves discussion, but consensus is the outcome of agreement, not the process.

deconstruct_text:
The word 'consensus' comes from Latin 'con-' (together) and 'sensus' (feeling). So literally, 'feeling together.' Think of a group that talks and ends up all agreeing—walang pikunan, lahat magkakasundo.

Picture a barangay council deciding on a fiesta budget. Sorry kung mahaba ang usapan, pero at the end, lahat nag-aprub—that's consensus. It's not a vote where the mayor overrules, but a shared 'yes' ng bawat lider.

Tandaan: 'Con-sensus' parang 'konsensya'—iniisip ang lahat, hindi iilan. Kapag may consensus, buong grupo ay sumasang-ayon.
next_time_rule: Consensus = 'pakiramdam na magkakasama.' If everyone's on the same page, that's general agreement. Don't mistake it for a vote or debate.
